Guidance & outlook: For Q1 FY27, we delivered 13% year on year growth in Strides Pharma Science Limited July 31, 2026 topline, supported by broad -based contributions across our business.
Despite additional operating and freight cost of ₹131m arising from ongoing geopolitical situations, our EBITDA margins were maintained at 18.2%, broadly in l ine with the exit levels of Q4 FY26.

We expect gross margins to remain in the 58-60% range. we reported ₹229.8 crore for the quarter, up 5.4% year -on-year, at an 18.2% margin - down 130 basis points year -on-year, but ahead of 18.1% in Q4 FY26.
Growth & demand: Our Ex -US markets continued to demonstrate strong momentum, delivering 17% year-on-year growth.

Coming to the US business, revenue for the quarter stood at ₹6,282 million or $68 million, reflecting a stable performance despite increased competition in certain products launched over the last few quarters.
Ex-US revenue grew 17% year-on-year to ₹5,875 million, with growth recorded across multiple geographies.
Margins & costs: Our objective continues to be to maintain gross margins within the 58% to 60% range, and deliver superior EBITDA margins driving operating leverage that translates into sustained EPS and P AT growth over the medium term.
Gross margin expanded 60 basis points year -on-year to 60.9%, driven by favourable business mix within Ex-US markets, and drove 14% growth in absolute gross margin to ₹770.2 crore.
Other operating costs (Ex freight) increased ₹29.0 crore year -on-year on account of higher manufacturing costs.
Capex & expansion: We now have multiple projects progressing across these technology platforms and continue to invest in building a differentiated pipeline that can support sustainable growth over the medium term.
At the same time, Africa delivered another strong quarter, led by the continued expansion of our Brands business.
So as far as the capex plan is concerned, the way we view capex is a combination of hard capex, maintenance capex plus the R&D.
Balance sheet & cash: After funding this working capital investment, we generated operating cash flow of ₹108.7 crore for the quarter, an EBITDA-to-cash conversion of 47%. we reduced net debt by ₹11.9 crore during the quarter, bringing closing net debt to ₹1,424.6 crore and net debt -to-EBITDA down to 1.52x, from 1.55x at the end of FY26.
From an overall perspective, the current net debt is about INR14.2 billion, like INR1,420 crores.
And also, you have to understand, Pratik, like when we started the debt conversation, the dollar was INR82.
Risks & challenges: Across the industry, we continue to see supply chain disruptions, elevated freight costs, longer transit times and inflationary pressures across multiple operating cost line items.

While Ex-US revenue for the quarter was at $63 million compared to $70 million in Q4 FY26, the quarter was impacted by certain supply chain disruptions which resulted in shipment delays across a few markets.
This reflects roughly ₹13.1 crore of incremental operating and freight costs attributable to Geopolitical disruptions, absorbed during the quarter.

EBITDA compounded at approximately 26% over the last 3 years, driven by the EBITDA margin expansion of 400 basis points to close FY26 at 19%.
Operational PAT has grown 18x over the last 3 years and EPS has increased to INR 56 for FY26, which is the highest for us with a strong exit run rate of INR14.7 per share in Q4.
